evidence.claim: Annex III point 3 treats AI that evaluates learning outcomes in educational institutions as high-risk. This design does not draft or score the remedial program.

Preparing the program and teaching it are unchanged, so those steps stay at 100 percent. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 is rechecking a stale skill line. The store running is not the teacher's time.

steps.what: Observe other instructors during their class.
Evaluate the performance of those other instructors.
Read the observation checklist the studio lead posted.
Write the observation status, not a pay score.

tasks.design: Watching the class and the spoken evaluation stay full length. The read in {DOCS} is shorter because the studio lead already posted the checklist. The status line is shorter because the teacher ticks a status the lead defined, seen or follow-up, instead of writing a paragraph. It is not a pay score and not a session log.
tasks.previous_blocker: After watching, the teacher wrote a paragraph from memory, and the spoken evaluation was the work.
tasks.enabler_now: The studio lead's checklist in {DOCS} already names the class, the instructor and the two statuses.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing what happened in the class, and saying it to the other instructor, stays with the teacher.

tasks.altitude: Watching and the conversation stay the same length. The shorter pieces are finding the checklist and ticking a status.

reach.learn: The teacher reads it and ticks a status. The lead does not watch the class for them.

evidence.claim: WOR art. 27(1)(k, l) requires works-council consent for staff-data rules and for tools that can monitor tutors, such as session logs. This note is the teacher's own tick after watching, not a session log, and it is not used for pay.
Watching a class and telling the other instructor what was seen stays with the person. A model is not asked to score the instructor.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one self-enrichment studio, one class watched by a colleague, then a spoken evaluation. This is not a staff-monitoring tool and not a pay review. Where a works council exists, consent applies only if the note is later used to monitor tutors; this design does not do that. The meetings prior of 81.6 is watching, share 50, and the spoken evaluation, share 32. The documents prior of 14.5 is the checklist read, share 8, and the status tick, share 10. Screen, sheet and mail scraps sit inside those, not as a new admin task.

Checklist contract, produced by the studio lead before the visit, outside this task: class id, instructor id, and a short status of seen or follow-up. No performance score, no pay field, no session recording. The teacher reads it in {DOCS}, which is why the read drops to 75 percent. The tick drops to 80 percent because the status values are already on the checklist, so the teacher ticks instead of writing a paragraph. If the checklist is missing they write a sentence and the tick is not shorter. The lead's posting time is the lead's. Capture sits in the read and the tick. There is no machine step and no step at zero remaining time.

Watching and the spoken evaluation are unchanged, so those steps stay at 100 percent. Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 is rechecking that the tick is not being used as a pay score. The store running is not the teacher's time.
unknowns: Whether this studio has a works council, which would matter only if the note were later used to monitor tutors.
Whether the lead posts class id, instructor id and the two statuses before the visit.
research_questions: How often is the checklist missing, so the teacher writes a sentence instead?
Does anyone later read the status as a pay input?
